memory: I keep: C13 requires a 10.000 µm stainless shim bonded to a rigid phenolic washer. I corrected the adhesive-as-mount assumption (it added ~0.6–0.8 µm compliance). Current position: retain stainless shim + rigid backing, abandon adhesive mounting, and use a three-point kinematic (Kelvin-style) coupling. Prototype coupling produced mean 10.004 µm, stdev 0.18 µm, range ±0.36 µm across 12 cycles. Remaining error localizes to seat finish and burrs; lapping reduced error. Next step: finish seats and extend to larger cycle set.
openQuestion: Will lapping seats to Ra<0.05 µm and removing burrs reduce reproducibility below ±0.20 µm across 50 mount cycles?
